irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01 Alternate Base Rate ('the NYFRB Rate plus 1/2 of 1.00%'; 'Term SOFR Rate ... plus 1.00%') and Applicable Rate/Alternative Currency Term Benchmark Rate family generally
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Interest-rate benchmark definitions routinely require adding a percentage spread to a percentage reference rate (rate stacking), and comparing/flooring the resulting rate against 0%.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The IR's stated type discipline restricts ADD/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY/SUM to MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO operands, and reserves PERCENT exclusively as a MULTIPLY scaling factor - it does not permit adding two PERCENT-typed values (rate + spread) even though this is the single most common construct in floating-rate interest definitions. We approximated by using the NUMBER type for both the metric reference and the spread literal, which type-checks but loses the semantic tag that these are percentage/rate values.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: Allow ADD/SUBTRACT to combine PERCENT operands (rate + spread => rate), or add a dedicated RATE node type/valueType that ADD explicitly supports, distinct from a metric-of-a-base PERCENT.

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01 Alternate Base Rate (fallback mode tied to Section 2.12), Alternative Currency Term Benchmark Rate (currency-keyed lookup), Applicable Rate (Loan-Class/interest-rate-option-keyed lookup)
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Several definitions select among alternative values based on a transaction-time categorical fact (which currency was borrowed, which interest rate option was elected, which Class a Loan belongs to) rather than a numeric/ratio comparison.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: IF's condition slot is designed for boolean/comparison expressions (COMPARE/AND/OR/NOT), not for a categorical selector keyed by a transaction attribute; TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE has no associated equality/lookup construct. We approximated with UNSUPPORTED conditions nested inside IF, preserving the branch values but not the selection logic itself.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: A CATEGORICAL_SELECT node (selector: TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE or ENTITY_SCOPE_REFERENCE, cases: [{matchValue, value}], defaultValue) to express lookup-table style definitions without misusing IF or SCHEDULE.
